3. What is the wall concept?
The Wall was the original idea for the home feed — like a locker-room wall everyone on the team can see. In the early builds it was one long page where the coach posted the week’s workout, the weekly challenge, and shoutouts, and athletes could see GRIT Cards and who was leading.

We took that single Wall page out and split it into tabs so it’s easier on iPhone — Athletes, Training, Homework, Mindset, Impact — but the idea is the same: the “Wall” is the shared team board. The Impact page is now where that Wall energy lives: weekly challenge, leaderboard, and GRIT Cards.

Supabase SQL — Athlete PIN login

Run this in Supabase → SQL Editor. It creates the athletes table, stores only a hashed PIN, and gives you a safe login function that never returns the hash.

SQL
-- 1. Enable hashing
create extension if not exists pgcrypto;

-- 2. Athletes
create table if not exists public.athletes (

How it works in the app:

  • Athlete picks their name → types 4-digit PIN → app calls verify_athlete_pin(name, pin)
  • If it returns a row, they’re in and their name shows at the top of Training
  • If it returns nothing, show “Incorrect PIN”
  • Never fetch pin_hash to the front end

4. Make it publishable to Supabase + live updates

The app’s save functions in this build are now structured in one place so they can swap to Supabase without changing the UI. Here’s the backend to publish it to:

Run this in Supabase → SQL Editor. It adds the training blocks + notes tables and turns on Realtime so when an athlete saves, you see it live too.

SQL
-- Enable Realtime + hashing (run once)
create extension if not exists pgcrypto;

-- Athletes already created in the last step.
-- If you haven't run that yet, run the athletes + verify_athlete_pin SQL first.

To go live:

  1. In Supabase → Project Settings → API, copy your Project URL + Anon Key
  2. In the app code, swap the built-in save functions to Supabase — the spots are marked in the code as:
    • saveAthleteProfile → supabase.from('athletes').update(...)
    • saveTrainingBlock → supabase.rpc('save_training_block', ...)
    • saveAthleteNote → supabase.rpc('save_athlete_note', ...)
    • saveFocus → supabase.from('grit_focus').upsert(...)
  3. For live updates, subscribe once per page:
JavaScript
supabase.channel('grit-live')
  .on('postgres_changes', { event: '*', schema: 'public', table: 'training_blocks' }, () => reloadBlocks())
  .on('postgres_changes', { event: '*', schema: 'public', table: 'athlete_notes' }, () => reloadNotes())
  .on('postgres_changes', { event: '*', schema: 'public', table: 'grit_focus' }, () => reloadFocus())
  .on('postgres_changes', { event: '*', schema: 'public', table: 'athletes' }, () => reloadProfile())

That’s what makes an athlete’s save appear live on your screen, and your coach edit appear live on theirs — no refresh needed.

  1. Deploy the front end anywhere that serves static files (Supabase Hosting, Vercel, Netlify, GitHub Pages) with those two keys as env vars. The app itself stays the same.

The 404 happens when any of these are true:

  1. File is not named index.html — if it’s named grit_wall_uploaded_...html or preview.html, GitHub Pages can’t find it → 404
  2. File is in a subfolder — if it’s in /docs/ or /site/ but Pages is set to / (root) → 404
  3. Pages isn’t turned on, or is pointed at the wrong branch/folder

Fix it in GitHub:

  1. Go to your repo > Settings > Pages
  2. Build and deployment > Source: Deploy from a branch
  3. Branch: main — Folder: / (root) — Save
  4. Make sure the repo root has only index.html — delete / rename any old grit_wall_...html files
  5. Wait 1-2 minutes, then open https://<your-username>.github.io/<your-repo>/ in a private / incognito tab and hard-refresh

If your URL shows .../index.html in it, remove that part — the clean repo URL is what should load.

do i leave it zipped?
Today

No — do not leave it zipped.

GitHub Pages can’t open a zip. If the repo only has a .zip file in it, it will 404 every time, because Pages is looking for an index.html and it can’t find one.

Do this:

  1. On your computer, double-click the zip to unzip it — you’ll get a folder with index.html in it
  2. Go to GitHub > your repo > Add file > Upload files
  3. Drag in just the index.html file itself — not the zip, not the folder
  4. Commit, then check Settings > Pages is set to Branch: main, Folder: / (root)
  5. Wait 1-2 minutes, then open https://<your-username>.github.io/<your-repo>/

Think of the zip as just the delivery box. You open the box, take the index.html out, and put that in GitHub.

If you already uploaded the zip to the repo, delete the zip file from the repo and upload the unzipped index.html instead — that’s what will fix the 404.

That’s the 404 then — if there’s no .html in there, GitHub has nothing to show.

Don’t worry, this is usually just one of these 3 things:

1. The extension is hidden

On Mac, Finder hides .html sometimes, so the file looks like it has no ending.

  • Mac: Finder > Settings > Advanced > turn on “Show all filename extensions”
  • iPhone Files: tap the file — look at the name at the top, it should end in .html
  • Windows: File Explorer > View > Show > File name extensions

Look again after that — you may see index.html was there all along.

2. You unzipped the wrong zip / wrong folder

Tell me what you do see in that unzipped folder — just the file names.

If you see something like:

  • grit_wall_uploaded_... with no ending → that is the html file, just rename it to index.html
  • A folder inside a folder → open the inner folder, the index.html is in there
  • Only .png / .txt / .md files → you got an assets-only zip, not the site zip
